request: A vacation calendar based on holidays and vacation requests, viewable for the whole organization, for several teams, or for specific people, drawn as a horizontal timeline where each row is a member and each column is a day. Holidays follow a country a manager states on the member, falling back to a country stated on the organization; the phone country code is not a source.
shardDecision: Read myself, no shards dispatched. The slice offered one shard per member, but this is a delta pass over 418 changed lines in a 1,293-line bundle and every defect in it crosses members: a Known Gaps row against the Summary two hundred lines above it, a Verification Plan row against a case in the same file and a requirement in another, a UI Description cell against the shipped members service, a Blast Radius paragraph against a Backward Compatibility item in the area README the bundle delegates to. A shard holding one member sees none of them, and the lead would be re-reading all three members anyway for the sixteen criteria the slice marks whole-bundle. I read all three members in full, plus specs/time-off/README.md, specs/organization/README.md and specs/user-management/README.md, both prior verdicts in .workflow/refine/time-off-01.probe/1 and .../2, and the diff of every commit in the range. I opened every file a claim rests on: apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts, apps/api/src/members/members.controller.ts, apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma, packages/validation/src/index.ts, packages/validation/src/roles.ts, packages/validation/src/holiday-messages.ts, packages/validation/src/reports.ts, apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.service.ts, packages/ds/src/components/reports/ReportControls.tsx. The pass this one follows is round 2, whose nine blockers the commit a64e65a says it repaired; seven are repaired in the text, two are not, and one repair is partial. F1 and F2 are the two the record claims and the document does not carry.

findings.claim: Both Known Gaps rows still describe the three-link chain this range deleted, and row 2 makes the safety claim the same document's Summary retracts. Row 2 calls `Organization.countryCode` 'the third link' and says 'the first two links behave exactly as they do today, so nothing regresses on the day the migration lands'; the chain now has two links, the first is a column this spec creates which is `null` on every row, and the source that behaved as it does today — `Account.phoneCountryCode` — is the one this spec deletes. Row 3 says 'the new chain can only widen it' against a Summary that says in the same file that the spec 'pays fewer holidays than today until somebody states a country'. A person planning the deploy from Known Gaps — which is where a reader looks for what to do on the day — concludes no action is needed, which is the opposite of what the Blast Radius exists to tell them. The round-2 verdict raised this as R5 and the repair commit's own message lists it as repaired ('two Known Gaps rows still made the "nothing regresses" claim the Summary retracts'); the text does not carry the repair.

witness.detail: sed -n '408,409p' specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.md prints both rows verbatim, still reading 'the third link of the chain', 'The first two links behave exactly as they do today, so nothing regresses on the day the migration lands' and 'the new chain can only widen it'. Against REQ-01-026 at :249-250 — 'resolve a member's holiday country as `Membership.countryCode` ... and as `Organization.countryCode` otherwise' — two links, and the Summary at :51-55 — 'this spec drops that source everywhere rather than ranking against it ... and pays fewer holidays than today until somebody states a country'. specs/time-off/README.md:139-144 is headed 'It can pay less than today'. git show a64e65a -- specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.md contains no hunk touching either row: `git log -p a08419dc..HEAD -- specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.md | grep 'third link\|first two links\|can only widen'` returns nothing.

findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite both rows against the two-link chain. Row 2's true reason is that both columns land `null` and the chain is evaluated on read, so nothing is stored wrong — not that nothing changes; the gap is the window in which members who had a phone country lose their national holiday rows, and what closes it is stating a country. Row 3 cannot say 'can only widen it', and its third link is now the second.

findings.symbol: Reaching the states the cases need / Not proven
findings.claim: The Verification Plan is the table that tells the next agent how to reach the states the cases assert, and it names a route to the member country that this spec's own rules make a dead end. 'A member with a country' routes through `updateAccountSettingsViaApi` with `phoneCountryCode` — a member seeded that way resolves to nothing under REQ-01-026, which drops the phone as a source. No row of the table reaches `Membership.countryCode` at all, and three cases need a stated membership country: TC-01-INT-12, TC-01-INT-25 and TC-01-E2E-08. The 'Not proven' row compounds it by describing a different spec: it calls `MemberProfile.country` 'the link this spec puts *first*' — the spec puts the membership column first and REQ-01-026's Decided sentence refuses the profile outright — and says 'TC-01-INT-12 is written for exactly that', a case rewritten in this same range to seed no profile country and to prove that a `BY` phone country reaches nothing. The round-2 verdict raised this as R7 and the repair commit's message lists it as repaired ('the Verification Plan still described a profile link that no longer exists'); the text does not carry the repair.

findings.suggestedFix: Replace the phone and profile rows with the routes this spec's cases actually need: stating a member's country through `PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/members/{memberId}`, marked not run because the field does not exist yet, and the organization country beside the row already there. Rewrite the 'Not proven' entry as the membership-country link, and stop attributing a profile-versus-phone seeding to TC-01-INT-12.

findings.claim: The area README the bundle delegates blast radius and backward compatibility to now counts the same set twice and gets two answers. A paragraph added in this range says two shipped member routes change shape; forty lines below it, Backward Compatibility item 3 still says 'No existing route, response field or `data-testid` changes', and the Frontend paragraph still says 'No existing screen's markup or test ids change'. Both are zeroes for a set with three members: `GET .../members/{memberId}` gains `countryCode` in its projection (REQ-01-045), `PUT .../members/{memberId}` gains it in its body (REQ-01-042), and the member detail About tab gains `member-country-select`. Item 3 is the row a person reads to decide which suites can be trusted untouched — it names the reports and holidays E2E suites as the enforcement — and the screen that changed is covered by neither.

witness.detail: sed -n '108,112p;151p;165,168p' specs/time-off/README.md prints '**Two shipped member routes change shape.** `GET .../members/{memberId}` gains `countryCode` in its explicit projection and `PUT .../members/{memberId}` gains it in its body', then 'No existing screen's markup or test ids change.', then '3. **No existing route, response field or `data-testid` changes.** The calendar's endpoint is new (proven: it answers `404` today), and the country endpoint is new. Enforced by the reports and holidays E2E suites, which are untouched by this spec and must stay green.' The `member-country-select` row is at specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.contracts.md:249, 'Member detail › About'. git show a64e65a -- specs/time-off/README.md added the 'Two shipped member routes' paragraph and touched neither item 3 nor the Frontend paragraph.

findings.suggestedFix: Item 3 and the Frontend paragraph state what actually changes on the existing surfaces — one response field, one request field, one new test id on the member detail screen — and say what enforces it, since the reports and holidays suites do not cover that screen.

findings.claim: The UI row rewritten in this range justifies drawing no read-only country control with a claim about today's authorization that is false for one of the two screens: 'the pages holding them are already refused to everybody else'. The member detail page is refused to nobody — `MembersService.getDetail` is documented and implemented as viewable by every role, and `view-list` is granted to `user` and `viewer` alike. So a `user` and a `viewer` do open the About tab, and the bundle never says what they see there. The same gap runs through the read: REQ-01-045 states the field only 'WHEN a caller holding `edit-detail` opens a member's detail', while the contracts' own section for that route says the projection simply gains the field and 'everything else it returns is unchanged', and the Routes row names no capability at all — 'capability checked in the service'. An implementer must choose between an unconditional field and one gated on `edit-detail`, and the two produce different response bodies for the majority of this product's roles. This is the half of round-2's R8 that its repair did not answer; R8 asked in as many words to 'say what a caller without `edit-detail` sees'.

witness.detail: Contracts :305 — 'Both country pickers are drawn only for the admin and manager who may save them; no role sees either control read-only, because the pages holding them are already refused to everybody else.' Against apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:305-306, the doc on `getDetail`: '`GET /members/:memberId` (spec 05 requirements 1-4, 11-13). Viewable by every role — the permission matrix only gates the two edit flags, never the read.' `CAPABILITY_MATRIX` in packages/validation/src/index.ts grants `view-list` to `user` (:~700) and `viewer` and `edit-detail` to neither. The unresolved audience is REQ-01-045 (specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.md:317-323) against contracts :113 ('The shipped projection gains one field (REQ-01-045). Everything else it returns is unchanged.') and contracts :12, whose Guards cell reads 'capability checked in the service' and whose Errors cell lists only 404, though the shipped route also answers 403 `MEMBER_MESSAGES.viewForbidden` (members.service.ts:313-316).

findings.suggestedFix: One repair covering both halves: say that the member detail page is open to every role and that the picker is simply not drawn for a caller without `edit-detail`, and settle the read — either `countryCode` ships in the projection for every caller who may read the member (and REQ-01-045 drops its `edit-detail` clause), or it is gated and the Routes row names the capability that gates it and the status a caller without it gets.

findings.claim: The matrix grants `ViewHolidays` for 'read the organization country' and no route exercises it. This range removed `ViewHolidays` from the only row that ever named it — the settings-country PUT, which now reads `ManageHolidays` alone — and added a read route for the member's country while leaving the organization's with none. The consequence is on the screen: the Holidays settings page draws a `Select` labelled Organization country whose value must be the stored `Organization.countryCode`, and nothing in this bundle returns it. `org-country-select` is a control the Screens section draws that no route serves; on first paint it has no value, so an implementer either invents a response field on `organization/03`'s shipping holidays read or adds an unspecified endpoint, and which callers may see the stored country is decided by neither this spec nor the matrix row that claims to govern it.

witness.detail: specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.md:81 — '| `ViewHolidays` — read the organization country | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |'. grep across the bundle finds `ViewHolidays` in exactly two places: that row and contracts :349, 'ViewHolidays opens the country field'. The Routes table (contracts :10-13) carries four routes — the calendar GET, the settings-country PUT, and the two member routes — and none reads `Organization.countryCode`; the PUT's Guards cell before this range read '`ViewHolidays` and `ManageOrganizationCountry` checked in the service' and now reads '`ManageHolidays` checked in the service' (git diff a08419dc..HEAD, contracts hunk 1). The control is at contracts :285-288 ('Gains one control above the existing country filter: a `Select` labelled **Organization country**') and :247 ('`org-country-select` | Settings › Holidays | present for admin and manager'), and TC-01-E2E-07 (cases :481-490) opens that page and sets it. `Organization.countryCode` is a column this spec adds (contracts :162), so no shipping route can be carrying it already: apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma's `Organization` model has no country column.

findings.suggestedFix: Say which read returns the stored `Organization.countryCode` and who may call it — a row in the Routes table for the shipping holidays read gaining the field, gated by `ViewHolidays`, is the shape the matrix already promises — or drop the `ViewHolidays` row from the matrix and say in the Screens section where the picker's initial value comes from.

findings.claim: Carried from both earlier rounds and still unconfirmed: on the day this deploys, every member whose only country was their phone's stops receiving their national holiday rows on Amounts Owed until somebody states a country for them or for the organization, and the fix is a manual step somebody has to own. The bundle records this completely and honestly — the Summary, REQ-01-026's Decided sentence, the area README's two directions with the probe's measurement, and Backward Compatibility item 2 — and no rule is missing. The newest spec governs; this is raised only so a person confirms the trade was meant. It is the one thing in this document that costs money if it was not.

Recorded as left for a person in .workflow/refine/time-off-01.fix.json (N4) and raised again as N4 by the round-2 judge.

findings.suggestedFix: None. Confirm the deploy-day dip is accepted and that setting the organization country in the same change window is an instruction somebody owns.

findings.claim: Cosmetic leftovers of the renumbering, reported because they are cheap to close and confusing to meet: the old `TC-01-INT-23`/`TC-01-INT-24` pair became `TC-01-INT-25`/`TC-01-INT-26`, so `TC-01-INT-24` now names no case at all (spec-lint counts 37 cases across ids 01-23 and 25-27), and the Acceptance Criteria table carries rows 18 and 19 between rows 11 and 12. Nothing is wrong and no criterion covers either; a reader looking for TC-01-INT-24 simply finds nothing, and the register has no rule about the ordinal order of a table's rows.
